name: Mount Airy

dates.altered: Interior of the main house gutted by fire in 1844 (the survey's data form); the Library's item lists '1844 Subsequent Work'.
dates.note: Four dates are on the record because four sources give them: the HABS data form prints 'DATE OF CONSTRUCTION (INCLUDE SOURCE) 1758'; the DHR entry says 'built 1748-58 by the wealthy planter John Tayloe II'; the Wikipedia infobox prints '1758–62' while its lead says 'constructed in 1764'; the Library's item says '1764 Initial Construction'. Recorded as the survey states it, with the others noted rather than resolved. The designer is likewise disputed: the survey form says 'attributed to John Ariss'; the DHR says the designer is unknown and the stone facades adapt a Gibbs plate, with William Buckland employed from 1762.

refs.title: Mount Airy, 361 Millpond Road (State Route 646), Warsaw, Richmond County, VA
refs.note: The item's note line reads 'Survey number: HABS VA-72 Building/structure dates: 1764 Initial Construction Building/structure dates: 1844 Subsequent Work'; call number HABS VA,80-WAR.V,4-. The dependencies are separate items (dairy VA-72-B va1223, smokehouse VA-72-D va1225, orangery ruins VA-72-E va1226, ice house VA-72-F va2472). The survey number is also printed on the data form ('HABS NO. VA-72').

note: Written 4 Sep 2026 from the WP-11.1 research pass; a new exemplar on tidewater-georgian. The survey's written data for this house is a one-page 1983 form, not a Part II description, so it carries no overall dimensions. It is stone where the node's recipe is brick, and it is here for the five-part composition the node's prose says Virginia and Maryland have more surviving examples of than any other region.
